message.content:
Civil law, also known as civil jurisprudence or civil law system, is a legal framework that governs non-criminal disputes between private parties. Its components can be broadly categorized into several key areas: | Component | Description | |-----------|-------------| | **Legal Sources** | • **Statutes & Codes** – Written laws enacted by legislatures (e.g., Civil Code, Commercial Code).
• **Case Law / Judicial Precedent** – Decisions from higher courts that guide lower courts.
• **Customary Law** – Long‑standing practices recognized as law. | | **Legal Subjects** | • **Persons** – Individuals and legal entities (companies, NGOs).
• **Property** – Real estate, movable property, intellectual property.
• **Contracts** – Agreements between parties.
• **Torts** – Wrongful acts causing harm.
• **Family Law** – Marriage, divorce, child custody. | | **Legal Processes** | • **Jurisdiction** – Determining which court has authority.
• **Procedural Rules** – How cases are filed, evidence presented, and judgments rendered. | | **Legal Remedies** | • **Damages** – Monetary compensation.
• **Injunctions** – Court orders to do or refrain from doing something.
• **Specific Performance** – Order to fulfill contractual obligations. | | **Legal Institutions** | • **Courts** – Trial courts, appellate courts, specialized courts (family, commercial).
• **Legal Professionals** – Lawyers, judges, notaries. | | **Legal Principles** | • **Good Faith** – Parties act honestly and fairly.
• **Equity** – Fairness and justice beyond strict legal rules.
• **Presumption of Innocence** – Not applicable in civil law; parties must prove their case. | | **Legal Documentation** | • **Contracts & Agreements** – Written or oral agreements.
• **Deeds & Titles** – Documents proving ownership.
• **Court Orders & Judgments** – Official decisions. | These components interact to form a comprehensive system that resolves disputes, protects rights, and ensures orderly conduct in society.
